names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 martie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Μαρτίου, «Άγιοι Χρύσανθος και Δαρεία», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first entry for the Julian 19 March on pravoslavno.rs, whose heading is „Свети мученици Хрисант и Дарија, и други с њима.“, where the form is the second of the two names the heading prints. The rank words Свети мученици stand at the head of the whole company and are left off, and nothing on the page gives this man an epithet or a city, so the bare forename is what the source gives.

death.note: saint.gr: «Στην συνέχεια έριξαν τους Αγίους Χρύσανθο και Δαρεία μέσα σε λάκκο και τους ενταφίασαν ζωντανούς. Ήταν το έτος 283 μ.Χ.», and it heads her «(; - 283)». doxologia.ro gave only the reign of Numerian, «(283-284)», so the interval the corpus first held was the reign; the Greek page states the year, and the two do not conflict.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 19 martie — «Sfânta Muceniță Daria»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιοι Χρύσανθος και Δαρεία»

attestations.note: «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Μαρτίου εκάστου έτους.» The page heads her «Αγιa Δαρεια (; - 283)» and closes the account «Ήταν το έτος 283 μ.Χ.», which is a year where doxologia gave only Numerian's reign. It makes her an Athenian — «η ωραία Δαρεία, η οποία καταγόταν από την Αθήνα και ήταν ειδωλολάτρισσα» — and gives the pair one joint service.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.04.2026 (19. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Хрисант и Дарија, и други с њима.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the other calendars already keep in these folders, and the same company: Rome, the reign of Numerian, the torturer who was converted by what he saw and died with his household, and Chrysanthus and Daria buried alive under stones. The heading names two and then „и други с њима“, and the body names three more — Claudius, Diodorus the priest and Marianus the deacon — and describes, without naming, Claudius's wife and his two sons. All eight folders the corpus already holds on this day take a row, which is how the rows already in them were written: saint.gr's own line for this family names all four of them together, and its line for the clergy names the other two. The Prologue's „283. и 284. године“ is the pair of years these folders already hold, so no date was touched. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinţilor Mucenici Hrisant şi Daria

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received crowns of incorruption from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Θείας πίστεως, τῇ ἐπιγνώσει, πᾶσαν ἔλιπες, πατρῴαν πλάνην, καὶ Χριστῷ κατηκολούθησας Χρύσανθε, ᾧ καὶ προσάγεις Δαρείαν τὴν πάνσεμνον, καὶ σὺν αὐτῇ τὸν ἀγῶνα ἐτέλεσας. Μεθ' ἧς πρέσβευε, δοθῆναι τοῖς σὲ γεραίρουσι, πταισμάτων ἱλασμὸν καὶ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr — Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως, on the page of Άγιοι Χρύσανθος και Δαρεία. It is the proper of the pair and names them both, so it stands on both folders; it is addressed to Chrysanthus and names her «Δαρείαν τὴν πάνσεμνον». The page's first apolytikion, Ἦχος δ’ «Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου Κύριε», is the common of martyrs and is not taken.

english.text: By the knowledge of the divine faith thou didst leave behind all thy father's error and didst follow after Christ, O Chrysanthus; and to him thou dost bring the all-revered Daria, and with her thou didst finish the contest. With her, then, entreat that forgiveness of sins and great mercy be given to those who honour thee.

hymns.text: Ὡς κρίνον χρυσαυγές, τήν ὀσμήν εὐσεβείας, ἐμπνεύσας δαψιλῶς, Χρύσανθε Ἀθλοφόρε, πρὸς γνῶσιν σωτήριον, τήν Δαρείαν ἐφείλκυσας, μεθ᾽ἧς ἤθλησας, καὶ τὸν ἀρχέκακον ὄφιν, τροπωσάμενος, πρός ἀκηράτους παστάδας, ἀξίως ἐπήρθητε.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος α’, Χορὸς Ἀγγελικός, on the page of Άγιοι Χρύσανθος και Δαρεία. It names them both and ends in the dual-plural, «ἀξίως ἐπήρθητε», so it stands on both folders.

english.text: Breathing out abundantly the fragrance of piety like a lily of golden light, O prizewinner Chrysanthus, thou didst draw Daria to the knowledge that saves; and having contended together with her and put the serpent, the author of evil, to flight, you were worthily taken up to the undefiled bridal chambers.
